answer: Interleaved Arrival Shape Gate. Each identity must submit its first transactions as a sparse plume of requests whose inter-arrival gaps fit a decaying schedule tied to account age; the gate scores gap variance and rejects bursts. Clones pay by having to wait out each gap in real time, so spawning N identities costs N times the serial delay. A canyon between allowed short-gap windows widens with recent failed entries from the same traffic source, slowing mass registration.
